question: e-11507

original_content.knowledge_point: Representing a Triple Integral as a Mixed or Repeated Integral
original_content.problem:
Find the missing limits in the repeated integral below

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x
$$

where $R$ is the type III region defined as

$$
R=\left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2, \: 0 \leq y \leq z+xz \right\}.
$$
original_content.worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z)  \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: u_1(x,z) \leq y \leq u_2(x,z) \big\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/0603bed12c6af74e46544d8bebc52362aed95a9a5ad7418ea4faaf228f3b5241.png)

 

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d y \right] \,\textrm d A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u_1(x,z) = 0, \qquad u_2(x,z)  = z+xz.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{S} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{z+xz} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D =\left\{ (x,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2 \right\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{2x+2}[{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{2x+2}{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem:
Find the missing limits in the repeated integral below

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x
$$

where $R$ is the type III region defined as

$$
R=\left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2, \: 0 \leq y \leq z+xz \right\}.
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Retain the defining inequalities of $R$ exactly. Ordered $z$ bounds require $x\le2x+2$, so $x\ge-2$. A nonempty $y$ fiber requires $(1+x)z\ge0$. For $-2\le x\le-1$, both $1+x$ and every allowed $z$ are nonpositive. For $-1\le x\le0$, keep only $z\ge0$. For $0\le x\le3$, the printed lower bound $z=x$ is already nonnegative. Therefore

$$\begin{aligned}\iiint_R f\,dV={}&\int_{-2}^{-1}\int_x^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx\\&+\int_{-1}^{0}\int_0^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx\\&+\int_0^{3}\int_x^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}$$

These three integrals cover the actual region with ordered bounds; boundary overlap has measure zero. For $f=1$, their volumes are $5/24$, $1/2$, and $903/8$, totaling $1363/12$. The source solution used $x\in[-3,3]$ and $z\in[x,2x+2]$ throughout, including reversed or empty fibers; its formal signed integral gives $111$ and does not integrate over $R$.

rationale: Preserve exact R; remove reversed/empty fibers using three actual base branches.
